messages.text: Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Doncaster Cup

metadata.summary: Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointing efforts at Royal Ascot and York to win the Betfred Howards Wright Doncaster Cup.
metadata.content: Doncaster Cup: George Scott's Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Town Moor Group 2 | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Doncaster Cup: George Scott's Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Town Moor Group 2 Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointment at York with a decisive victory in the Doncaster Cup; Also on the card, Final Objective got up in the final strides to deny Crownbreaker in the Flying Childers Stakes Friday 11 September 2026 15:54, UK Image: Caballo De Mar won the Doncaster Cup under Oisín Murphy Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointing efforts at Royal Ascot and York to win the Betfred Howards Wright Doncaster Cup. Questions had been raised over whether the five-year-old still had the stomach for the fight after coming home last in the Gold Cup and stopping quickly before finishing fourth in the Lonsdale Cup at York. But after taking up the running a furlong from home on Town Moor under Oisín Murphy, the George Scott-trained stayer proved his doubters wrong, pulling away from Beylerbeyi to land odds of 5-6 favourite by a length and a quarter. The race had been robbed of its likely favourite after Queenstown was pulled out and there was also drama beforehand when the Emmet Mullins-trained Winday gave trouble at the start. Having worked himself up into a sweat, he failed to the fire in the race itself, finishing a tailed off last of seven. metadata.content: Rangers vs Celtic: Martin O'Neill reveals 'general behaviour' message from police ahead of Old Firm League Cup clash | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Rangers vs Celtic: Martin O'Neill reveals 'general behaviour' message from police ahead of Old Firm League Cup clash Celtic face Rangers at Ibrox in Sunday's League Cup quarter-final; there will be no away fans after SPFL ruling; Mika Baur is available for the Hoops despite missing training; Martin O'Neill's side have won all six of their Premiership games this season Friday 11 September 2026 15:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill admits it will be strange to face Rangers at Ibrox with no away fans after the SPFL imposed a ban Martin O'Neill revealed Celtic were given a "general behaviour" warning by Police Scotland ahead of Sunday's League Cup quarter-final against Rangers at Ibrox. There will be no Hoops fans in the 50,000-capacity stadium at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants. The spat is partly a result of the last Old Firm clash in Govan in March, which was marred by fans' disorder as Celtic won the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup quarter-final on penalties after a goalless 120 minutes. messages.text: Inside the Solheim Cup: How players embraced 'insane' first-tee experience

metadata.summary: Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist said that the Solheim Cup first tee would be 'the place to be in the golfing world,' with that pre-tournament assessment spot on as she witnessed a spectacle unlike any other in the women's game.
metadata.content: Solheim Cup: How Team Europe and Team USA stars embraced first-tee party and 'insane' atmosphere at Bernardus Golf | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup: How Team Europe and Team USA stars embraced first-tee party and 'insane' atmosphere at Bernardus Golf What was the first-tee atmosphere like at the Solheim Cup? How a party atmosphere at Bernardus Golf brought an entertaining start to Team Europe's bid to regain the trophy in the Netherlands; watch the Solheim Cup live on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Friday 11 September 2026 14:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Megan Khang tee off in style at this year's Solheim Cup, after she hyped up the crowd to encourage more noise Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist said that the Solheim Cup first tee would be 'the place to be in the golfing world,' with that pre-tournament assessment spot on as she witnessed a spectacle unlike any other in the women's game. The horseshoe-shaped grandstand around the first tee at Bernardus Golf was close to capacity long before daylight, with nearly 3,000 spectators - and plenty more along the fairway - creating a party-like atmosphere of noise and excitement. United States captain Angela Stanford danced onto the tee after emerging from the tunnel, a walk Charley Hull said earlier in the week was like 'entering an arena', with vice-captains - from both sides - doing their best to make things even louder. messages.text: Sky Sports agrees three-year US Open extension

metadata.summary: Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal, ensuring Sky Sports and NOW remains the exclusive home of the tournament in the UK and Ireland until the end of 2030.
metadata.content: US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030 | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030 Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to broadcast the US Open; 2026 competition reaches thrilling conclusion at Flushing Meadows this weekend; watch Aryna Sabalenka take on Elena Rybakina in the women's final on Saturday, followed by the men's final on Sunday Friday 11 September 2026 14:26, UK Image: Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal, ensuring Sky Sports and NOW remains the exclusive home of the tournament in the UK and Ireland until the end of 2030. As part of the partnership with the United States Tennis Association (USTA), Sky Sports will retain exclusive live coverage of all men's and women's singles, doubles, mixed doubles, juniors and wheelchair competitions throughout the three-week tournament. The agreement was negotiated by the USTA's media rights partner, IMG. Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms. This year's coverage has featured augmented reality graphics, enhanced data integrations, in-depth touchscreen analysis and behind-the-scenes content, bringing fans closer to the action than ever before. messages.text: Man City's midfield options prove Rodri is replaceable after all

metadata.summary: By Enzo Maresca's own admission, Manchester City "complicated" their 2-0 win over Porto in the Champions League on Tuesday. The patchiness of their performance led Alan Shearer to call Maresca's side "weak" on Prime Video's co-commentary.
metadata.content: Man Utd vs Man City: Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez are the perfect answer to Rodri's summer exit | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Man Utd vs Man City: Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez are the perfect answer to Rodri's summer exit In the battle of expensive midfield makeovers, Manchester City's trio look the most complete, with Ayyoub Bouaddi the latest newcomer to impress Enzo Maresca; Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez have also made excellent starts in the wake of Rodri's exit Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Friday 11 September 2026 15:46, UK By Enzo Maresca's own admission, Manchester City "complicated" their 2-0 win over Porto in the Champions League on Tuesday. The patchiness of their performance led Alan Shearer to call Maresca's side "weak" on Prime Video's co-commentary. City did fail to consolidate their advantage until late on, but never really looked in danger of squandering it. Statistically, Porto were restricted to scraps. For a team who had not been beaten at the Estadio do Dragao throughout the whole of 2026, there were few clear-cut chances to speak of. Not a single shot on target. Man City's superbly balanced midfield made sure of that. The danger here is of course to compare what City are serving up under Maresca with performances of the past, where everything flowed simultaneously around Rodri in the style of Pep Guardiola. Russell is looking to hit back after losing out to championship leader Antonelli last Sunday at Monza and started the Spanish Grand Prix weekend perfectly as he outpaced Antonelli by 0.286s.
